"But soon, we will ascend to a higher world and start to travel to more worlds of even higher ranks.
So get a feel for it now, for you will be getting more later."
He turned his focus back to the next set of messages that were all about the world.
Basically, this is a world ruled by beasts and monster races.
They have different kinds of beasts, each with a powerhouse rooted in this world.
However, the strongest existence is the Tyrant Orc King Balma, a powerful being whose tyranny spreads far and wide.
He rules over the majority of this world, and while there are other powerhouses, because of his strength, they can only bow to him.
This caused Kent to sense something fishy and true to his feelings; when the description of the forest before them appeared, he got his answer.
"There is good news and bad news," Kent smiled, causing his legion to look at him strangely.
"The one we are coming to save is in the deepest prison in that direction.
However, before we can get to her, we must first kill three Orc generals, who are the level three Sovereigns.
Now, the bad news.
This world is ruled by someone we cannot survive a single attack from.
And if we kill even one of the three Level 3 Orc Generals, that being will sense it and come after us."
Kent was smiling while saying that.
One could already see the craziness in his eyes.
"I don’t know about you, Master, but I want to see such an existence and perhaps exchange a punch or two," Kaizo said, and like a maniac, Kent’s smile bloomed.
"Let’s move out.
We have three orcs to kill."

chapters.title: Chapter 383: Saving Dori (2)
paragraphs: "I say we should just eat those fox girls we picked up three days ago," a tiger beast said to another tiger standing atop a wall, acting as the guards of the bandit hideout.
"The leader said they will be sold to the merchants tomorrow, that the Orc King wills it," the second tiger beast said. They are both in their humanoid forms, so they can wield weapons.
They are wielding two large Sabers.

"If it’s an order from the Orc King, then there is no debating that. After all, we work for him, and I heard he is planning on invading another world soon. He had figured out a way to teleport his forces there."
"We will get to have a good battle then. It’s been a long time since I had a good battle with anyone."
The two tigers kept talking while maintaining awareness of their surroundings.
Meanwhile, two kilometres away from them, Kent and his legion stopped and looked at the tall wall guarded by Root Transcendent guards.
"I can see eight of these tigers standing on all four sides of the wall," Sylara said, her red eyes shining.
"That is an easy fix then," Kent said, looking at Nyxira. "Can you handle them?"
"I can," the Soul Sentinel answered without hesitation.
"Then we will wait for your signal." Nyxira nodded and moved with the shadows. Soon, she was nearing the wall, where the two tigers remained oblivious.
"I say we wait this one out, and if nothing comes within the hour, we can just take a nap," the tiger beast said and was about to add something when a dagger appeared at the throat of his friend.
Before he could shout, his friend was dead, and his throat was also slit.
Nyxira materialized from his shadow and glided toward the other side of the wall, keeping her body wrapped in shadow so nobody could sense her presence.
But even if anybody could sense her, it would be the three orcs who were now drinking in a certain room, unaware of the danger approaching them.
It took less than a minute, but all eight guards were killed, and Nyxira gave the signal.
"You know the plan. The rest can be killed on sight, but the three orcs are to be subdued first. We will kill them after we are done with the mission."
They nodded.
Uncle Drew retrieved his mask and put it on giving him a terrifying presence. Strangely, his strength skyrocketed the moment he wore the mask.
He then snapped his fingers, and eight figures, all clad in dark clothes with hoods and masks on their faces, appeared.
Two are Root Ascension, and six are Root Transcendent.
"See you all soon." Both Uncle Drew and his eight hell demons vanished, and the next second, an explosion rocked the fortress of the Crimson Vipers.
"Time to smash things, y’all!" Kaizo was the second to leave, and just as he arrived, a level 3 Sovereign orc appeared with a frown on his ugly face.
Kaizo wasted no time and punched at him, sending him flying. Kent shook his head, watching his brute land that punch before, he also blinked away.
By the time he arrived, Sylara had also isolated another orc, and Veydris was facing the third.
Saden and the sentinels, along with the four battle dolls, also went into action, and just like that, the fortress of the Crimson Vipers was under siege.
"Tempest Fist!" Kaizo roared, and like the brute he was, his fist crackled with lightning as he descended on the orc, who had taken up a rather large spear, his body exuding a potent yellow energy.
"Kaizo, don’t let him stab you with that spear; it is poisonous," Kent cautioned his brute undead, who nodded and distanced himself just fast enough for Kent to unleash his Rapid Sword Slash.
While the attack was effective in pushing the orc back, it did little to no damage. But that was to be expected, considering they were fighting a sovereign.
Of course, Kent wasn’t disappointed; he just never expected his attack to have such little effect.
However, the moment that attack pushed the orc back, Kaizo got an opening, and he didn’t miss.
"Piercing Fist!" Lightning coated his arm and solidified into pointed gloves.

"Eat that, sucker!" His fist went through, and like being pierced by a spear, he dug a hole into the chest of the orc, who screamed in pain after landing outside the fortress, clearing a wide area of the pink forest.
Kent raised his sword and channelled his energy into it. Then, taking a powerful swing, a wide arc of energy shot out.
The orc, seeing the attack, swung his spear to meet it, but before he could completely defend himself, he noticed that Kent had vanished from the air.
The next second, a painful cut landed on his exposed knee, drawing yet another cry of pain.
"Just who are you people? Don’t you know we are under the authority of Lord Balma? You can’t kill us!"
The orc, who wasn’t even allowed to attack by Kent and Kaizo, spoke, only to feel Kaizo’s fist slam into his face again.
"Don’t worry, bro, we don’t really care about your boss. So keep quiet and suffer," Kaizo said with a smile. Even Kent couldn’t hold back his laughter.
This caused the orc to roar as his body burst into energy, now radiating a deeper shade of yellow, showing he had activated an enhancement skill.
The two became alert; their opponent was now much more dangerous.
Meanwhile, Sylara, who was facing the second orc, seemed to be having a field day with the pitiful bastard.
Her claws were radiating potent red abyssal energy as she cut and stabbed the pitiful orc who was unfortunate to have faced such a monster.
On the body of the orc, one could see deep cuts, showing she wasn’t holding back her attacks. Of course, she wasn’t. The being before her was a Sovereign who had reached level 3.
Playing around would just be stupid.
Nearby, Veydris had already severed one arm of the orc. Blood poured from the orc’s body as he staggered, weaponless.
The battle hadn’t even begun in full circle, yet Veydris, Abyss Knight had already ended his battle by severing the weapon-wielding arm of the orc.
Veydris was done with his mission. The arm that once held the weapon was gone.
To prove it, Veydris swung his void blade unleashing a wide sword arc.
The sword’s arc vanished the moment it left the sword.
Before the orc could sense it, a powerful slash struck his chest, sending him flying. He crashed to the ground, unconscious.

chapters.title: Chapter 384: When Night Riders Fight
paragraphs: Kent and his team chose to attack just as the night was rising.
This wasn’t because they wanted to use the cover of darkness. No, this was a deliberate plan to allow his two-night riders to harness their powers, as they were meant for the night.
Uncle Drew and Saden are immortals at night, meaning the chances of them dying are less than 1% during the night.
So the moment they attacked, their full strength surged, and riding the night, Saden was like the harbinger of death.
She moved with the night, and her arrows, forged from the flames of hell, were the only things visible in the air.
She was tasked with handling the transcendent with the three soul sentinels and the four battle dolls; that was exactly what they were doing.
"Devouring by the night."

Saden was solely using that skill since it practically handed her supreme authority over the night, preventing those within the range of this skill from seeing anything, even if they possessed night vision.
So, essentially, she was using the night against her opponents, rendering them blind.
But while that was happening, she was also doing something else. She was knocking a few out. However, she wasn’t doing so randomly.
No, she was executing something only night riders could do.
Every night, the rider possesses an ability called Mark of Destinies. This mark allows them to identify those who can play a role in their strength.

Back when Uncle Drew sent those eight attackers who came after Kent to hell, he used that ability to determine their worth, and the answer to that question was the purple marks now glowing on the foreheads of 13 Transcendent Beasts currently unconscious on the ground.
She was acting on the command of Uncle Drew, who was also doing the same thing with the ten Ascension-stage beast-kin.
Thankfully, only six had to be killed, as they didn’t have destinies tied to them.
But while that was the case, there was yet another development between these two that would have caught anyone’s attention.
While Saden was a Peak Sage, from the moment Uncle Drew arrived from hell, she ascended from the Root Sage stage to the peak of Root Great Sage.
She even surpassed Kent in that regard, for Uncle Drew had now become a Transcendent.
As to how that was possible, it was due to the red string now linking Saden and Uncle Drew as they fought and killed.
This string acts as a link, transferring energy between them. This means that as Uncle Drew grew stronger, so would the riders under his command.
But it wasn’t a one-way channel. Aside from Uncle Drew providing her energy, she also supplied him with energy, and now, as they fought, one could tell this channel was opened and working like a dam.
In fact, Kent still doesn’t understand how Uncle Drew became a Transcendent. But then he mentioned time runs faster there, so it wasn’t impossible.
Saden and the sentinels were killing much faster, showing they were all warriors in their own right. The battle dolls were also killing their fair share.
However, the main reason why they were killing faster, considering the staggering number of Transcendents and small fries, was because Veydris had joined them.
Veydris had already handled the Sovereign he was tasked with, so he is helping them.
Uncle Drew was the second to finish his task, so he and the hell demons joined the fray, and soon, the echoes of cries and anguish could be felt.
Meanwhile, Sylara flew down from the holding the orc, which was being suspended by her claw at the shoulder joint.
The lady had indeed destroyed the orc, proving she was a merciless being.
Meanwhile, Kent and Kaizo were having a field day with the last orc. Kaizo was now clad in lightning armour and was using Overdrive, boosting his speed by several folds.
Meanwhile, Kent’s skin was covered in dark gold dragon scales, and both his horns and wings were active.
When the orc activated its enhancement skill, Kent and Kaizo also activated theirs, and thanks to that, they managed to subdue the last orc, even following in Veydris’s footsteps.
Kent severed its arm, and Kaizo blinded one of its eyes.
"BOOM!"
A body slammed to the ground as Kaizo landed one last powerful attack on the last orc. It passed out immediately.
"That was satisfying," Kaizo said, deactivating his armour. Kent simply smirked and deactivated his dragon enhancement skills.
By the time they arrived inside the fortress, every last beast was dead, with only 21 of them unconscious. Of course, the three orcs weren’t included.
"Young Master, I would like to check if these three are suitable to be turned into hell demons," Uncle Drew asked, and Kent nodded.
After a while, Uncle Drew shook his head.
"They are not worthy," Kent said with a smile.

"At least you have 17 Transcendents and 4 Ascensions meaning you will be getting 4 soverigns soon if things go well. I guess this time, when you leave, it will be months or years before we see you again."
"Indeed. But I won’t leave until the fourth Rider awakens," Uncle Drew replied, his smile hidden behind his mask.
"Don’t worry about it. The moment she wakes up, I will invoke her true name," Kent said, glancing at Sylara and then at the bloodied orc.
"Was that really necessary?" he asked, causing Sylara to turn and look at the orc.
"Perhaps I may have gone a little overboard. But it’s not my fault. A battle without blood is meaningless to me, so I had to shed his blood," she replied, causing Kaizo to feel his blood run cold.
He could testify to her ruthless fighting style.
Kent smirked and turned to the entrance, where Saden and Nyxira were escorting three people. One was a young girl with a ponytail and skin covered in scales.
But with one glance, Kent knew she was in disguise. She was bound in a green, chain-like rope that suppressed one’s cultivation.
The moment these three people saw Kent and his legion, they became scared. However, the ponytail girl smiled when she saw Kent’s face.
"You must be Dori," Kent said.
In response, the rope binding her hands loosened, and like a spoiled child, the loli jumped into Kent’s arms.
"I missed you, Master. I never thought we’d meet this soon. Of course, I calculated a 32% chance you’d come to rescue me the moment you found out I was captured.
Let me guess: Akira found you, and thanks to Gaia, you’re here now. Of course, there’s a 74% chance the Quest Pool gave you a quest to come save me.
In other words—"
"Nice meeting you again, Dori," Kent interrupted, knowing that, as Akira and Gaia had said, she would ramble nonstop if he didn’t cut her off.
After all, she was a Mind Weaver who weaves complex plans and overthinks everything. Talking about statistics and mind-bending is her strong suit. If Kent were to allow her, she would speak nonstop.
They are in a no man’s world, so he is not ready to talk about statistics.

chapters.title: Chapter 385: Dori, The Mind Weaver
paragraphs: After Saden and Nyxira brought Dori and the two ladies out, the two passed out when they saw Sylara.
A few seconds later, the other two soul sentinels also returned with seven more, and like the first, they lost consciousness when they saw Sylara.
She looked terrifying, and the blood energy around her was enough to scare anyone.
"Poor souls... They were taken from their families, and there was nothing any of them could have done," Dori said, looking at the nine figures on the ground.
"Do you know them?" Kent asked.
"I only know these two," she replied, pointing at the two ladies who had been brought out with her. They were both Foxkin.
"The one with dark hair is the daughter of a leader of the foxkins, and that is her servant."
"Were you taken with them?" Kent asked.
"Yes. I was their advisor of sorts, helping them handle some diplomatic matters. We travelled for 3 years, but on one of our trips, we encountered an unfortunate incident about a year ago.
Unfortunately, we wandered into this path, and that’s why we’re now here."
"1 year is a lot. They could have sold or perhaps kill you long ago, however they didn’t. I guess that’s to be expected from people who seem to be working for someone," Kent nodded.
"I guess it was good we came when we did, else you would have been sold. However, how did you find yourself in this world?" Kent asked.
"That’s a long story," Dori said, scratching the back of her head.
It turned out she had found herself in that world after discovering they were under the suppression of a tyrant.
When she arrived, the Tyrant Orc King Balma held supreme authority over the world, but thanks to her scheming and planning, a resistance started to rise.
The Foxkin leader Hkun led one such resistance.
He had recently stepped into the ranks of a Spirit Lord. Though he hadn’t reached the level of the Orc King, hope arrived when the Catkin also welcomed their first Spirit Lord.
She and the princess had gone there to negotiate an alliance, and if that was successful, their chances of reclaiming their lands would be high.
Thankfully, their alliance became a reality.
Next was the Tigerkin, who also wanted to reclaim their lands.
However, on their way to negotiate the alliance, the Rabbitkin found them first, and after a week of playing hide-and-seek, they ended up here.
Their families had no idea this had befallen them, and thanks to her being a Mind Weaver, though she couldn’t go against these people, she managed to draw suspicion away from the Foxkin.
This meant that the resistance would rise within the next 15 years if the timeline was correctly tracked.
"So you were building a resistance against the tyrant king," Kent said with a smile. "I never expected you to be a rebel. I guess appearances can be deceiving."
Dori’s cheeks turned red at the compliment. "I just wanted to help them, considering the previous world I came from was also one of beastkins."
"So now that you are free, what do you intend to do?" Kent asked. She looked at the two ladies and then the seven with them and sighed.
"They must first be returned to their homes. However, 15 years from now, a great battle will happen, and they will lose.
For the moment the Rabbitkins sense our presence near the territory of the Tigerkin, the Orc King was made aware.
However, since you are here now, I can say if the resistance doesn’t do anything stupid before the 15 years, which I calculated will be the tipping point, then you can turn the scale for them."

Dori smiled. "I hope Master wouldn’t turn down a good fight." She knew Kent from all his incarnations since she had been there from the beginning, so asking this question was from years of experience.
"Don’t worry; I will transcend within the next six to ten years, so by then, I will be in the element that will allow me to handle this Balma dude.
We can only think of a way to set him back a few years." Kent smiled and looked at Veydris.
Dori also looked at the Metal Knight, who had Void Energy around him.
"Does the Master want to use poison on the Spirit Lord?" Dori asked, and Kent nodded.
Securing a poison wouldn’t be hard for him, considering there are dozens in the tower shop and millions in points to purchase.
Applying it is where the problem is. Kent would have to get close, and that is not an option, so the next best thing is Veydris, who could use the Void to attack.

chapters.title: Chapter 386: Remember My Name
paragraphs: "This is the bone-corroding poison. Veydris will apply it to his sword since he is immune to it. This is the weapon we will be using against the Orc King," Kent said to the two undead before him.
"You two will immediately attack when he arrives. Remember, it’s just one attack, so make it count. The moment your attack happens, Veydris will also attack.
It doesn’t matter whether it works or not; vanish into the tower immediately after your attacks."
They nodded.
"Very well, the moment of truth will arrive soon." After instructing them, he looked at Dori. "I will send you away now. Your sisters are waiting."

"Okay, Master, just be careful. The odds are heavily against you, so be very careful." After nodding to her words, Kent sent her away, and she appeared at the mountain garden where Gaia and Akira were waiting for her.
"Looks like life hasn’t been nice to you, Dori," Gaia said, hugging her like a bear.
"I may have been out of my element for a moment there, which landed me in that mess. But life has been good since the last time we met." Akira was hugging her from behind, too.
"I see you finally got the tower up and running. Master must really be thrilled."
"He doesn’t remember that side of him yet. In fact, he had just recently started remembering his life as the Slave Swordsman," Gaia responded.
"He would probably twist your ear if he heard you call him Slave Swordsman," Akira said, and Dori smiled.
"Then thank you both for helping Master come to get me, though the chance of him learning about me in the coming days was high even if you two hadn’t said anything."
"And what makes you think he would have learned of your existence?" Gaia asked.

"Have you forgotten which of us found him first in his life as Lord Genesis, the Divine Swordsman? It was I, and back then, he knew I was a Mind Weaver, for I helped him in his path as the first true swordsman.
So whether you said anything or not, he would have realized, and knowing him, the universe had already made contact, so he would have asked for a way to save me.
Either way, he would have come for me," Dori said, and the two sisters just smirked.
"Sometimes, you are just too smart for your own good. Now, let’s sit back and watch how Master makes his first overpowered enemy."
Gaia waved her hand, and the scene around them changed, showing them the pink forest where Kent was about to execute the three Sovereign-stage orcs.
Kaizo and Sylara were hidden out of sight but nearby, while Veydris was inside the void. He didn’t have much to say, but he knew what he must do.
"I really hope I don’t die from being this reckless," Kent muttered. Then he commanded the doom shards, driving them through the necks of the three, killing them instantly.
The moment they died, he took their bodies and blinked away, appearing a couple of kilometres from the execution site.
Two seconds went by, and nobody appeared.

The seconds started to tick, and soon, ten seconds passed. Kent, who was farther away, began to wonder if the being would come at all. But after 30 seconds and still no one appeared, he could only sigh.
He had expected a quick response, but that didn’t seem to be the case.
This made him change his mind, and he was about to abort the mission when the space cracked open, and from the deep, dark crack, a figure walked out.
It was a dark figure with white marks lining his body, giving him an aura of pure strength and danger. He stood about three meters tall, with arms as thick as an adult’s thigh.
He had two white horns.

The moment he appeared, his gaze fell on the destroyed fortress, causing his blood to surge. However, just as he was about to act, lightning flashed through the clouds, and a large fist emerged from the lightning storm that formed on the horizon.
"Mountain-Breaking Fist!"
Kaizo’s voice filled the space as his fist descended on the figure, who looked up and smirked. He raised his hand and flicked his finger, sending a beam of white energy at the fist.
The moment it connected, the fist was destroyed, but Kaizo just smiled, for he saw a red light flash through the surroundings. Before the Orc King could sense it, Sylara was a meter from him.
She stabbed her claw at the Orc King, who held a calm expression. However, just as he was about to attack, Sylara’s red eyes brightened, and the Orc King closed his eyes.
She didn’t attack with her claw again; instead, she turned into a dust of red energy right when a purple sword arc arrived behind her.
At the same time, the Orc King, who had been mind-attacked by Sylara, opened his eyes just as the sword arc appeared before him.
There was no escaping it, so he crossed his arms over his chest and defended against the sword arc. However, a small cut appeared on his arm, making him scoff and ready to kill the three bugs.
Yet, when he scanned the surroundings, only one person was sensed—a demi-dragon hovering in the air with his horns and wings activated, his skin covered in dragon scales.
The Orc King immediately used his energy to bind him, but just as he took hold of Kent, his energy was cancelled, and the dragon smiled at him.

"You might want to take a look at that arm," Kent said, pointing at the Orc King’s left arm, which was now turning red and had already spread past his shoulder, meaning cutting it off was no longer an option.
The poison has taken effect.
"Who are you, and how dare you poison me? Do you not know who I am?" The Orc King’s energy exploded.

"I’m afraid using your energy only hastens the effect. Relax for now—for the next few years, you won’t be able to do anything. While this poison can’t kill you, it will at least prevent you from killing anybody."
Kent smiled.

"Be sure to relax and wait for me. I will return, and when I do, your tyranny will come to an end." He deactivated the dragon enhancement, showing that his true human appeared, and he smiled now that his work was done.
"Be sure to remember my name... Kent Madson, the Chaos Dragon." He winked at the Orc King and snapped his fingers, vanishing from sight.
He had to know that the figure before him was still a Spirit Lord at the 6th level despite cancelling his energy and poisoning him.
The Orc King screamed, causing his tyrannical energy to fill the entire forest, flattening it. However, he coughed up blood, showing the poison was spreading faster.
"Kent Madson... I will hunt you down." He vanished, and as Kent said, he wouldn’t be going anywhere for the next few years.
At the universe’s core, the lady watching Kent’s life unfold smiled and chuckled. "He never changes, always looking for trouble with beings he can’t measure up to..."

chapters.title: Chapter 387: Hidden Reward, World Teleporter
paragraphs: After leaving the last badass words with the Orc King, Kent found himself back inside the Mountain Garden, panting for breath.

He may have acted badass, but the danger he had just escaped from was one that he never wanted to feel again. The Orc King was someone just three steps away from stepping into the Heavenly Ascension realm.
Just as Core Formation is the peak of a medium world, the Heavenly Ascension stage is the peak of a high world, and Kent had just spoken such bold words to a being of that calibre.
That in itself is a badass move that cannot be replicated.
It was like staring into the face of a god and giving him the middle finger
It was the true definition of badass.
However, that doesn’t mean he was in his element while facing such a being. It was more like he had faced danger itself and walked away, sweating profusely.
Thankfully, he was smart enough to use the Chaos Dragon bloodline in its full 8% awakened stage. That was what prevented him from breaking down when the Orc King appeared.
The chaos energy was one that transcended all, so having a bloodline of chaos was enough to make him unafraid in front of such harrowing dangers.
"I don’t want to feel that powerless ever again. Next time, I want to look down on him and step on his face if possible," Kent said before falling onto his back and bursting into resounding laughter.
"But that was awesome!" he shouted, causing the three little cosmic beings inside the garden with him to roll their eyes.
⟪I suspected something like this would happen,⟫ Akira said to her sisters through telepathy, looking at Kent now basking in the glory of outwitting the Orc King.
⟪Statistically, this was something anybody would feel proud of,⟫ Dori said.
⟪Master is just at the Great Sage stage, yet he went against a Spirit Lord. I say we give him the benefit of the doubt.⟫

⟪I guess you’re right. But we have to admit, that was a close call. Had Sylara not coordinated well with Veydris, that sword attack wouldn’t have connected,⟫ Gaia said, having watched the short yet decisive attacks perfectly coordinated by the three warriors under their master’s command.
Kaizo was the first distraction, meant to make the Orc King realize he wasn’t in any danger, as the attack from Root Transcendent held no real power.
However, the main attack came from Sylara and Veydris.
Sylara has a skill called [Cursed Gaze]. It’s both a soul and mind attack. When used, her red eye shines and unleashes a haunting cry that can shatter the will of anyone.
However, the being she used it against was just too powerful, so it only made him close his eyes. But that was exactly what she was aiming for.
He used her claw as the second distraction in that world. So the moment the Orc King aimed for the claws, she unleashed the Cursed Gaze, and thankfully, he closed his eyes for a second.
But Veydris had already made his move, and that wasn’t a simple sword attack. All his accumulated Void energy went into it, and thankfully, that attack worked.
It was a light wound, but it was enough to let the poison affect him. All Kent had to do was enrage the already enraged Orc.
That was all he needed to do.
Thankfully, Kent knew all the right words to say, and that was where the main attack came into play. The Orc King used his energy, which hastened the effect of the poison.
However, in that split second, he unleashed his energy, and despite Kent cancelling it using [Rule Breaker], it still affected him in ways he never knew possible.
But he didn’t falter and left a mark on the heart of the Orc King, making him regret ever meeting the demi-dragon being who is now being sought in many locations on Fedora.
Thankfully, there were no dragons there, so he went after the wyverns and the like that had some strands of dragon blood in them.
But their loss is deserved, for all of them are his allies and have done more damage to the innocents, so their loss is indeed justified.
⟪Now that he has a taste of such power, I think we all know what follows. He will start training and looking for ways to grow stronger, rising until they notice him.
That would be dangerous, and we wouldn’t want what happened last time to repeat again, right?⟫ Gaia said, and the two sisters nodded.

⟪This time, we will ensure his growth is absolute. There will be no room for errors like in previous times. This time, the tower is ready, and all tools are prepared. Since we three are here, unity has been achieved.
We can now continue what we started billions of years ago with Master, making him rise beyond the strength of this universe and fight the creatures of the Beyond.⟫
⟪Let’s do that.⟫
The three ladies continued to stare at Kent for a while until he lifted himself up and sat down.
"We should do more missions like this one," Kent smiled and turned to his rewards.

He took out the Dungeon Seeker card upgrader he received and immediately upgraded the dungeons to SS-rank, meaning he now had 12 SS-rank dungeons where he would be facing 12-floor bosses, all at the Sovereign stage.
After that, he retrieved the schematic and handed it to Akira. "You and Dori can play with it."
When that was settled, he retrieved the last item. It was a rectangular-shaped object with a button and a small screen that displayed a single name on it.
"Fedora."
Kent quickly appraised it, and the description was one he never saw coming.
⟪Name: World Teleporter⟫
⟪Grade: Mythic (Upgradable)⟫
→ For every world you visit, the World Teleporter will record the coordinates and later help you teleport there.
→ It only requires a strand of your energy to work.
A smile spread across his face as he began planning how to make the Orc King bleed in the years to come.

It was a rectangular-shaped object with a button and a small screen that displayed a single name on it.
"Fedora."
Kent quickly appraised it, and the description was one he never saw coming.
⟪Name: World Teleporter⟫
⟪Grade: Mythic (Upgradable)⟫
→ For every world you visit, the World Teleporter will record the coordinates and later help you teleport there.
→ It only requires a strand of your energy to work.
A smile spread across his face as he began planning how to make the Orc King bleed in the years to come.

chapters.title: Chapter 388: Meeting In-Person for the first time
paragraphs: ⟪Looks like the universe is spoiling you, Master,⟫ Akira said with a giggle as she tinkered with the World Teleporter.
"It’s only natural to spoil such an amazing person like myself. Have you ever heard of a Great Sage facing a Spirit Lord before?" Kent asked with a smile.

⟪I guess you’re right, but this is just too much for someone at your level. Do you have any idea what many have to go through and what amount they have to spend just to do interplanetary teleportation?⟫ Gaia asked.
"They are not me, so their loss."
⟪This is indeed a good item. It will help us check up on the state of affairs in the world of Fedora and perhaps create some hindrance for the Orc King.
This will help us buy more time for the resistance. ⟫ Dori analyzed the importance of the teleporter and already saw the potential it held.

"That is exactly what I was thinking. With this, we can go there and perhaps make him vomit blood. For now, he will be in a comatose state for at least five years. By then, I will be close to reaching the peak of this world.
I’m sure by then, I can face him and not run to my mommy."
After playing with the teleporter for a while, Kent moved to the Legion Tower, where Veydris was in hibernation mode, and Kaizo, just like his master, was basking in their success.
As for Sylara, she was drinking blood from a Tigerkin she had taken from the battle.
Uncle Drew was also around. He was the last to teleport back into the tower after dropping off all the prisoners.
Luckily, their families were still around, so they would find them sleeping a few meters from their homes the next day.
"Kaizo, you should probably rest for the next few weeks. I’m afraid after handling things on the outside, the next few years will be spent moving from one battle to the next."
"Bring it on, Master. I am ready for anything," Kaizo said confidently. Perhaps after getting beaten in the coming dungeon battles, he would learn to cool off a little.
After talking with Uncle Drew for a while, Kent moved back to the Sword Tower to use one of the three Memory Keys to unlock more memories of his life as Jest.
He planned to unlock one and assimilate its effects before moving on to the next. But he intended to use all three before the Pill Master competition, which was coming up in seven days.
However, the moment he arrived inside the Sword Tower, Selene called him—the ladies had awakened thanks to the Celestial Dew of Rebirth he had given them.
He quickly went over, and the moment he arrived inside the garden, he saw the ladies seated around a picnic basket, eating fruit.
Nara and Zaila were surrounded on all sides, smiling and talking to each other.
It was a nice sight to behold, and Kent, who saw how happy they were now, could only curse the late sect master for making them suffer all these years.
"Ladies," Kent said, walking toward them. Thankfully, his ladies had chosen to put aside their shamelessness and wore clothes so they were all decent and well-dressed.
Of course, they wouldn’t wear such clothes outside, but inside, they were free to wear revealing outfits. Nara and Zaila were no different in that regard.
Their shapes and assets are nearly showing for the Dragon Lord to appraise. However, Kent wasn’t being shameless in that department today.
"Kent!" Val was quick to jump into his arms, welcoming him as if they had been apart for years.
In truth, the mission in Fedora had taken just 17 hours. But that was 17 days for them, so it was indeed a long time for all of them.
Kent hugged her and made sure she was comfortable before looking at Nara with a smile.
"So, this is you. I didn’t get a good look at you the last time, and since the previous meetings were with a bat, I have to say, you’re not bad-looking at all," Nara said, now full of energy.
"It’s only natural for someone like me to be handsome," Kent replied, making Nara laugh.
"Handsome, capable, and shameless," Nara said, turning to look at her sister. "I approve."
Mara blushed upon hearing her sister’s words. However, a warmth spread across her chest as she listened. Nara was her idol.

She was the one who had protected her when they were in danger. Nara had used her body as a shield against attacks from all the dangers they had faced together. Now, hearing her approve of her relationship, Mara felt overwhelmingly happy.
"I guess now that I have your approval," Kent said, turning to look at Mara, "you won’t be getting any sleep."
Mara had to hide her face behind her sister, blushing so profusely that if her disciples were to see her, they would probably draw their weapons and charge at her.
The Mara they knew was not the same as the one blushing profusely now.
"I want to take you all somewhere, but since this is a picnic, let’s finish the basket first," Kent said, sitting down in the waiting arms of his ladies. The picnic resumed.
"Zaila, huh? A beautiful name," Kent said, making the spear genius, who was supposed to have died twenty years ago, smile.
"Thank you for saving us," Zaila said.
"Don’t worry about it. It was the right thing to do," Kent replied, causing his ladies to roll their eyes.

"You ladies don’t have to be like that. We all know Camilla is a beauty, and having such a beauty by my side is a blessing. Making sure she becomes happy is what I wanted, and now, look at her—she’s over the moon."
Camilla, just like Mara, was also blushing. She had already confessed to Zaila about her decision to take Kent as her man, and just like Nara, Zaila had approved.

Naturally, Zaila had tried to encourage her master to get into the market decades ago, but Camilla had never listened. So, hearing that she now had a man in her life, Zaila couldn’t have asked for a better welcome-home gift.

They ate the fruits, joked, laughed, and reminisced about many things. When they were done, Kent teleported them to the tower city, where they were thrust into the most elegant city they had ever seen.
The moment they appeared, a loli in a cute little suit approached them. "Welcome to Gaiaville, the dream city."

chapters.title: Chapter 389: Placing A Hit On His Head
paragraphs: Among all the things Kent expected, Gaia in a suit wasn’t one of them. Yet here he was, staring at the small human who was looking surprisingly cute inside her little suit.
"Gaia, what are you doing?" Kent couldn’t help but ask, smiling.
"You said the city is my responsibility, so as the mayor of the city, it’s my job to welcome its residents," she said, making Kent roll his eyes.
He finally understood why his ladies rolled their eyes when he did something shameless. Right now, Gaia was the one being shameless, so he just rolled his eyes.
"She looks cute... where did she get such a design from?" Selene asked, touching the collar of her suit.
"It’s a design from my world," Kent said, making Zaila and Nara look at him strangely.

"He is not from this world, big sister. Kent is from another world far from this one," Mara said, and her sister, alongside the disciple of the Spear Gate Master, could only look at Kent for confirmation.
"She is telling the truth. I am from a place called Earth, and back there, this is how corporate ladies dressed. It’s a rather nice fashion decision if you ask me," Kent smiled.
"Gaia, since you are the mayor, ensure these beauties have the best time here," Kent said. Gaia nodded and clapped. Immediately, two more lolis in suits appeared, making Kent smile.
Akira and Dori looked at their master with a pleading gaze.
"Gaia, stop bullying your sisters," Kent said, knowing they weren’t there of their own accord, despite him knowing these were just a strand of their consciousness.
"They owe me, so I am cashing in that debt to ensure your ladies have the best time here," Gaia said, maintaining a business expression before turning to the ladies.
"How long will you be spending here?" she asked. In return, Selene looked at Kent and asked, "How long until the pill master competition?"
"Less than seven days from today, so you have 144 days to spend here if you want to come and watch," Kent answered, and the ladies nodded.
They all planned on going to see him dominate the alchemy world, too. He had already shaken the hearts of many, and now, he planned on shaking them more.
"However, Nara should come back in the next 120 days to meet someone," Kent added. They nodded, and Gaia took them into the city, where they started their vacation.
Kent wanted to join them, but he also had things to do now that he had received an SSS-ranked quest he couldn’t just ignore.
Of course, the moment he was done with what he had planned, he would pay them a visit and spend some quality time with them.
However, right after the pill master competition, he will be going back to the God Realm to satisfy a goddess who is currently immersed in research about all her sisters.
Now that they have awakened their True Names, they have all changed and, as such, have become new people. She was looking to understand more about them and how best to help them even further.
Vexthra is determined to ensure her man is surrounded by powerful ladies all around
The moment Kent left the tower city, he appeared inside the Sword Tower, where he sat down on the Enlightenment Stone and began to meditate.

Meanwhile, somewhere far from the Divine Palace Sect, three figures, each at the peak of the Root Ascension stage, were seated in a private room inside one of the most secure inns in the Kingdom of Varyndor.
They are clad in dark clothes, and each has a hood over their head. There was one seat reserved, indicating they were waiting for a fourth person.
Indeed, a few minutes into their wait, a figure appeared out of thin air and sat down. The newcomer was a beautiful lady with graceful features.
However, the air around her was that of a Level 7 Root Sovereign who had fought countless battles and killed thousands.
She was formidable, and the moment she entered the room, the three figures became alert.
"So, that bastard sent you three to the meeting instead of coming himself," she muttered, then sighed.
"Very well. I asked for this meeting simply because I want someone dead, and it must be done in the most efficient way possible."
"My lady, who do you want dead?" one of the three asked. Though he spoke, he wasn’t entirely confident, as the lady before him was not someone to underestimate.
"He goes by the name Kent. He is an inner disciple in the Divine Palace Sect," the lady revealed, making the three turn and look at each other.
"Is there a problem?" the lady asked.
"No, my lady. It’s just that asking us to handle a Root Sage—or perhaps now a Great Sage—seems rather unexpected. At any time, you could kill him with a flick of your finger, so why ask for us?"
"My employer wants him dead, but not by any of our hands. It must be done by an external party. This is where you three come in. So, do you have any more questions, or is he someone you can kill?"
"We will get it done, my lady. But do you have a timeframe for the mission?"
"It must be done before the sect competitions in three months," the lady said, and the three men nodded.
"Then tell your leader that if he fails this mission, he should forget about our alliance." After saying that, she vanished, leaving the three hooded figures behind.
"What now? Killing that brat will be simple enough, so why ask us to do it?" one of them wondered. After a moment of pondering, they all sighed and vanished from the room as well.
After the lady left, she appeared inside a new room many minutes later, where another figure could be seen seated in a chamber filled with cultivation treasures.
He was cultivating intently.
"Is it done?" The voice belonged to a man.
"Yes, my lord. Kent Madson will be dead within the next three months," the lady bowed and soon vanished.
"The Hand shall prevail," the man said before returning to his cultivation.

chapters.title: Chapter 390: The Next Memories
paragraphs: Kent spent three good days meditating. This was something Dori told him to do to prepare him for what he was about to see in his memories.
It was also a way for him to save his already-attained memories before new ones came.
After he was done, he took out one of the three memory keys meant to help him retrieve memories of his past life as Jest, who was known as Lord Genesis.
He was the first person to have surpassed the Sword King stage and risen to the peak, becoming the first-ever Celestial Sword God.
Now, Kent wanted to know more about that life and learn from it.
The first set of memories was about his life from when he was born inside the slave mine. He saw his life progress through the years until he became old enough to scale the Doom Wall.
When he escaped and became a swordsman at the Genesis Light Sword Sect, he began to rise, and finally, he reached the stage where he was recognized as a powerhouse.
However, while he was at the Sword Saint stage and was hailed as a genius, he never wanted to remain there.
The strongest in the entire world was a Sword King, and that was the last stage for them. That was the stage believed to be the peak.
But Jest knew better.
He knew there was nothing like the peak, for one can keep rising, so he started chasing paths that would take him beyond his current stage and even push him past the Sword King stage.
After years, he realized there was no such way available in the entered world.
That was when he decided to create his own path.
The memory ended there, and Kent, now holding the next memory key, sighed.

He knew that if just a prelude to the real path could push his sword path to that stage, who knows what would become of him when he finally received the true memories of him taking a step to create the Genesis Sword Path?
"This should be good, then," he said.
He pressed the key against his forehead, and it entered his mind.
Since he had already unlocked the Lord Genesis memories, he could now, as casually as he wanted, access the memories using the keys.
The moment he pressed the key against his forehead, the memories began to flow into his mind.
Jest spent 20 years travelling the world in search of a path that could elevate him beyond the Sword King stage.
However, even after meeting the infamous Mountain-Cleaving Sword King, the strongest in the entire world, he couldn’t find what he was looking for.
For a moment, he was disappointed.
That was when he made up his mind.
He knew that if he wanted to rise above that stage, he must create his own way. So, he took permission from his master and left the Genesis Light Sword Sect, travelling to the Sword Valley.
The Sword Valley is one of the most dangerous places left behind from the Primordial Era. It was one of the few remnants of that ancient time.
It was believed that during the Primordial Wars, two powerful swordsmen—rumoured to have risen beyond the Sword King stage—fought in that valley.
Some may call it a rumour, but most consider it a legend. The legend speaks of a legendary battle that lasted for 66 days straight before one of them fell.
However, to show respect to the one who fell, the victor stabbed his sword into the ground and never picked it up again.
Many say that had it not been for that battle, true swordsmen might have risen from the first era, the Primordial Era, as it was believed that these two were among the true swordsmen.
But since they fell, the sword was the only remnant left behind.
Perhaps it was magic, but the sword intent and qi used in that battle still linger in the air to this day.
It is said that all who venture into the valley have a high chance of attaining enlightenment and even going as far as obtaining a sword skill if they are lucky enough.
Skills used in that infamous battle were captured in the sword energy in the air, waiting for the lucky ones to come and learn.
Many rumours also suggest that the sword path used by the two swordsmen was captured within the sword that was stabbed into the ground.
So, all those who ventured there were not only after those sword skills but also the sword paths said to have been stored inside the sword stabbed into the ground.
However, nobody has ever gotten close to the sword, for it was never meant to be approached by the unworthy.
Naturally, Jest wanted to go there and see if the rumours were true. So he set off, and after a year of travelling, he arrived at the Sword Valley, where he was thrust into a world of danger.
The air was filled with the potent energy of the sword, and the remnants of previous sword attacks and echoes of those battles still lingered.
Powerful beasts also took refuge in that space, so Jest had to be extra careful not to fall prey to any of them.
Three years into his exploration, he encountered the first sword skill that wasn’t aiming for his life. Before this fateful encounter, all the sword moves he had encountered were deadly.
However, that was to be expected, considering this was a place where two swordsmen—believed to be beyond the Sword King stage—had fought.
Additionally, aside from the beasts, there were sword moves that could easily kill. However, the beneficial ones were reserved for those who shared a destiny with them.
The moment such a move was learned, it would transform into a dangerous sword technique capable of killing.
That was how Jest learned the Limitless Sword Arc Domain skill. It was a sword skill that, when used, would create a 100-meter domain of pure sword arcs fashion from sword intent and Qi.
Those caught within were destined to have a very bad day. Of course, it came at a cost, but Jest was happy to have learned such a sword move, and so he kept moving.
For five years, he wandered the Sword Valley, searching for the supposed sword stabbed into the ground, but he came out empty-handed.

Yet, his determination never wavered. So, for two more years, he continued his search. On one fateful day, he encountered a dangerous beast he knew he never had the strength to fight against, so he had to run.
Twelve hours—that’s how long he was chased. But in the end, he fell into a vortex pit, and with regret and failure in his eyes, he drowned in his sorrow.
"Welcome, slave," a voice said.
Then he woke up.

The moment he pressed the key against his forehead, the memories began to flow into his mind.
Jest spent 20 years travelling the world in search of a path that could elevate him beyond the Sword King stage.
However, even after meeting the infamous Mountain-Cleaving Sword King, the strongest in the entire world, he couldn’t find what he was looking for.
For a moment, he was disappointed.
That was when he made up his mind.
He knew that if he wanted to rise above that stage, he must create his own way.
So, he took permission from his master and left the Genesis Light Sword Sect, travelling to the Sword Valley.
The Sword Valley is one of the most dangerous places left behind from the Primordial Era.
It was one of the few remnants of that ancient time.
It was believed that during the Primordial Wars, two powerful swordsmen—rumoured to have risen beyond the Sword King stage—fought in that valley.
Some may call it a rumour, but most consider it a legend.
The legend speaks of a legendary battle that lasted for 66 days straight before one of them fell.
However, to show respect to the one who fell, the victor stabbed his sword into the ground and never picked it up again.
Many say that had it not been for that battle, true swordsmen might have risen from the first era, the Primordial Era, as it was believed that these two were among the true swordsmen.
But since they fell, the sword was the only remnant left behind.
Perhaps it was magic, but the sword intent and qi used in that battle still linger in the air to this day.
It is said that all who venture into the valley have a high chance of attaining enlightenment and even going as far as obtaining a sword skill if they are lucky enough.
Skills used in that infamous battle were captured in the sword energy in the air, waiting for the lucky ones to come and learn.
Many rumours also suggest that the sword path used by the two swordsmen was captured within the sword that was stabbed into the ground.
So, all those who ventured there were not only after those sword skills but also the sword paths said to have been stored inside the sword stabbed into the ground.
However, nobody has ever gotten close to the sword, for it was never meant to be approached by the unworthy.
Naturally, Jest wanted to go there and see if the rumours were true.
So he set off, and after a year of travelling, he arrived at the Sword Valley, where he was thrust into a world of danger.
The air was filled with the potent energy of the sword, and the remnants of previous sword attacks and echoes of those battles still lingered.
Powerful beasts also took refuge in that space, so Jest had to be extra careful not to fall prey to any of them.
Three years into his exploration, he encountered the first sword skill that wasn’t aiming for his life.
Before this fateful encounter, all the sword moves he had encountered were deadly.
However, that was to be expected, considering this was a place where two swordsmen—believed to be beyond the Sword King stage—had fought.
Additionally, aside from the beasts, there were sword moves that could easily kill.
However, the beneficial ones were reserved for those who shared a destiny with them.
The moment such a move was learned, it would transform into a dangerous sword technique capable of killing.
That was how Jest learned the Limitless Sword Arc Domain skill.
It was a sword skill that, when used, would create a 100-meter domain of pure sword arcs fashion from sword intent and Qi.
Those caught within were destined to have a very bad day.
Of course, it came at a cost, but Jest was happy to have learned such a sword move, and so he kept moving.
For five years, he wandered the Sword Valley, searching for the supposed sword stabbed into the ground, but he came out empty-handed.
Yet, his determination never wavered.
So, for two more years, he continued his search.
On one fateful day, he encountered a dangerous beast he knew he never had the strength to fight against, so he had to run.
Twelve hours—that’s how long he was chased.
But in the end, he fell into a vortex pit, and with regret and failure in his eyes, he drowned in his sorrow.
"Welcome, slave," a voice said.
Then he woke up.

chapters.title: Chapter 391: First Encounter with the Sword Dao
paragraphs: Jest woke up on a crystal floor.
The moment his eyes adjusted, he managed to take in his surroundings, and it was that of a serene environment filled with a powerful energy he immediately recognized.
"Sword Intent, Sword Qi, and another..." He tried to comprehend that other energy, but he couldn’t. However, just the two were enough to tell him he was inside a place that could not be joked with.
It was all crystal, and the light filling the place was coming from a distinct source, so he started to follow it. It took him just a few minutes to approach the light.
However, from a few kilometres away, he heard a voice come from the source of the light.
"Welcome, Slave."

Jest stopped his advance and looked toward the light, trying to adjust his vision to see if he could make out the entity that spoke, but no matter how long and hard he tried, he couldn’t figure out the entity.
"Who is there?" Jest asked.
"Shouldn’t a slave bow down to his master?" the voice spoke again.
"I am a slave no more. And if you don’t stop calling me a slave, we are going to have a problem," Jest said, and the entity’s light shone almost as though it had taken offence to his words.
"A slave that doesn’t know his place dies pitifully... You know that, right?"
Jest chuckled. "A slave who wills to be free wouldn’t hesitate to sever his master’s head if that means he can forever be free," he replied.
"Then have you severed your master’s head? I can tell you are still shackled, meaning you are still a slave."
"Being shackled is a reminder of the promise I made to myself. I could have removed the slave mark and forever rid myself of my past, but that would mean I would forget my roots.
I was a slave, still a slave, but will be a slave no more. So stop wasting my time and tell me who you are and why I am here."
Jest wasn’t angry. It was far from that.
The mention that he was still a slave was something he never wanted to forget.
One of the first things he did after escaping the slave mine was to find out who the owners were, and from what he found, it belonged to the Seven Ancient Immortal Clans.
They are a force he cannot measure up to. So, while it aches his heart knowing his people are still suffering, there is nothing he can do about it... now.
But he never forgets that the main reason he aspires to become strong is to free them and kill every last one of these slavers. That was why he wasn’t angry when the entity called him a slave.
It reminded him of who he was and is and that he wishes to be no more.
But that doesn’t mean it sounded pleasant, either.
"You are determined. I saw how you struggled over the years, chasing after something that isn’t there. I saw how you weaved your way through thorns just to find what wasn’t there.
So I brought you here to tell you this: what you are looking for doesn’t exist. What you aspire to create isn’t possible, so free yourself and let fate rule it all."
Those words stung, yet Jest merely smiled.
"A wise man once said, what isn’t there and what can be are one and the same. You called me here because you aspired to be, yet you don’t have the faith to become.

I don’t know you, but I know me, and I know what I am after is possible. The question now is, are you a loser who doesn’t believe in himself, or are you a legacy that wants to live on for years to come?"
Naturally, Jest spoke those words, but he wasn’t the one who said them. It was as if an unfathomable presence moved his lips and brought out his words.
This was something he would only realize years later.
The entity didn’t speak for a very long time, and Jest, too, didn’t move for that duration. However, after a year of silence, the entity spoke again.
"You seek a path to the apex. I can give you that. I can give you the key to walk that path. But as to whether you get there, that will depend on three things.
First, your determination to get where you want to go.
Second, your intent to rise to that level of authority and harness the strength that comes with it.

Third, your will to never shake and never falter, regardless of the obstacles you have to break. These are the only three things you need to aspire to walk the Sword Dao, and that is the key you seek.
Go back and resume your journey. You are already on the path, but whether you can walk it, as I said, will depend on the three things."
"Who are you?" Jest asked. Just now, when the entity spoke, it was as if his eyes had been opened, and he could finally see.
In fact, his eyes had been opened, and he could see the strings of the Sword Dao, one of the mysteries of the universe that, to this day, hasn’t been fully understood.
"I don’t have a name; I only have a symbol. I don’t come from anywhere, for I am everywhere. I aspire to be known, followed and chased after.
I am the Dao of the Sword, the path you seek to walk. Remember your determination to walk, your intent toward what you are walking towards, and your will to never stop walking.
These are the only things you need.
Go back, and may fortune smile on you, Slave. We will meet again someday, and when that day comes, I hope you will finally figure out what it is you are truly chasing after."
For a minute before he was sent away, the light cleared, and an entity clad in otherworldly battle armour, wielding a giant sword, smiled at him.
Kent snapped his eyes open, and immediately as he did, the entire Sword Tower shook as a powerful sword energy burst out of his body and eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 392: Sword Gaze
paragraphs: In the path of the sword, there are many aspects one must possess to be able to walk it.
Sword Qi, Sword Intent, and Sword Body are the three most common ones known to many. However, there are others, and the more you possess, the easier it becomes for you to walk the path.
One such aspect is the Sword Gaze.
Just as the Weaver Gaze is meant for artisans, array masters, and formation experts, there is a gaze for swordsmen, and it’s called the Sword Gaze.
This allows one to see the strings of sword energy in the air and around them. That is its primary use, to see the strings of sword essence and master them.
Of course, there are many ways to utilize it.
However, at that very moment, Kent’s eyes were changing colours between red and golden, neglecting his natural purple colour.
This caused him to clench his head, writhing as the pain that reached down his spine overwhelmed his mind.
Dori, Gaia, and Akira appeared inside the tower, and despite the overwhelming Sword Qi and Intent in the air, they remained unaffected. Instead, happy and proud smiles could be seen on their faces.
⟪Master is awakening the Sword Gaze aspect,⟫ Gaia said with a happy smile.
⟪That is quite early for him this time, but I guess this is good. With the Sword Gaze, mastering the sword wouldn’t be much of a hassle for him,⟫ Dori added.
⟪I am more interested in him using it in combat. Reading the patterns of his opponents would come in handy.
But if he manages to learn just one Sword Gaze skill for combat, perhaps he will become much more evil than the last time⟫ Akira giggled.
While the ladies were imagining things, Kent was suffering on the ground for four good hours before the pain finally subsided.
But the moment it calmed down, his eyes snapped open, and a wave of Sword Intent and Qi flashed out, powerful enough to shake the heart of anyone.
Just looking at the set of red-golden eyes said it all. Those eyes weren’t a normal set of eyes. They were the eyes that showed how sharp his focus had become.
They also revealed how lethal his Sword Intent and Qi had grown.
Kent stood up and summoned his sword. The moment the sword inside its sheath entered his grip, the energy around him began to stir.
His Sword Intent and Qi started to rise.
Initially, it was at the 6th level, but after the first memory, it had moved to level 7. Now, after the second memory, his Intent and Qi rose to the 9th level, climbing two levels.
However, while he was just a step away from awakening Profound Sword Qi and Intent, someone possessing that would still struggle under his Intent.
This was because of one thing that was about to happen to him.
The moment the sword appeared, he looked at it and sat down.
Then, slowly, he began to draw the sword. However, the moment the sword was halfway out of its sheath, his body froze, and an air of enlightenment surrounded him.
Kent had entered his first enlightenment, and from the energy surrounding him, one could tell something profound was happening to him.
⟪Gaining enlightenment right after awakening his Sword Gaze is a recipe for disaster,⟫ Akira giggled.
⟪Dori, what are his chances of learning at least a Sword Gaze ability?⟫ Gaia asked. Dori was the best person to answer, considering this was her field.

⟪The chances of the master learning a Sword Gaze ability is 51%. The reason he might fail 49% of the time is because he is inexperienced. He is still too green, for he has never really faced much hardship for a while now.
However, the 51% comes into play, considering he has just recalled a memory of his time with the Sword Dao.
Though it’s just a memory, we all know the master’s memories aren’t ordinary, so we can only hope that comes into play.
But he has a higher chance of learning a Sword Gaze ability—and a powerful one—if he indeed was taken to such a place.⟫
The Cosmic Weaver and Soul Weaver nodded.
Dori, being a Mind Weaver, could casually see Kent’s memories, and from what she saw, the memories he just recovered were of his time with the Sword Dao.

Of course, Kent had given her permission, as the three were essentially there to help him. But now, the remaining question was whether or not he had what it took to comprehend whatever skill he would be presented with.
⟪I miss this. I miss us together, making sure the master gets the best out of everything,⟫ Gaia said, smiling.
⟪I miss this too. The master said family is everything, so it’s good we are finally together and reunited with him, even if he hasn’t remembered us yet.
I’m sure the moment he awakens the memories we’re in, he will finally start utilizing our abilities more.⟫
⟪That is going to be fun then. I can already see a lot of things he will require us to do. I most certainly want to remain busy and working always.⟫
The three ladies looked at their master, who was frozen in his enlightened state, and a wicked idea came into Gaia’s mind.
She extended her hand, and three different coloured markers appeared in her palm.
⟪You are evil, Gaia, but I like it,⟫ Dori giggled. She took one marker from Gaia, and Akira also took one.

⟪I calculate him being in the enlightened state for 90 days minimum, so we have time on our hands. I say we paint the Guy Fawkes mask on his face. This time⟫, Dori called dibs on the mischief they were about to commit.
⟪Fine. But this is only because we are giving you a welcome home gift. Next time he enters enlightenment, we will paint the bone mask,⟫ Gaia said.
Then they moved and started decorating their master’s face. Perhaps from past experience, they were having so much fun painting Kent’s face.
At the core of the universe, the beautiful lady giggled, amused.
"These children never learn. But then again, I guess their master also never learns." She covered her mouth as if trying to hide her smile.
A dim golden light flashed across her eyes.
"When he is punishing you, don’t come running to me," she said, but Gaia just smirked as she decorated Kent’s face.

chapters.title: Chapter 393: The Gaze Enlightenment (1)
paragraphs: The sword Dao is a mystery.
Nobody knows how far it extends.
Those who reached the peak of the sword path awakened the Sword Will to its apex, yet they never spoke of its origins or the vastness of its power.
However, it is believed that all Dao stems from the same source, and that source can be accessed through the realm of enlightenment.
It is the only place that one can genuinely say they have met the Dao even if it was just in the will merely in the air.
Everyone experiences enlightenment differently, and each person has eleven chances—or more—to trigger enlightenment at various stages of their path.
Kent triggered his first enlightenment, the [Enlightenment of the Gaze], which came as a surprise.
He never expected it, nor did he anticipate awakening such a power. Now, he has entered the realm of enlightenment, standing beneath thousands of tombstones.
"Enlightenment, huh?" Kent muttered, gazing at them. The moment he appeared, he instinctively knew where he was, what he must do, and how long he would remain there.
"Two years to master as many skills as I can... That’s convenient," Kent smiled.

"Until now, learning how to unleash sword attacks using my eyes wasn’t something I saw coming. But I guess I must do it. Two years will pass in the blink of an eye, and as Elsa said, time runs faster here."
He sat down and closed his eyes, sending his consciousness to closely examine the tombstones, each holding a unique skill that cannot be replicated.
The moment he learns a skill, it will vanish, never to return.
"Void Severance," Kent muttered, examining a tombstone that seemed to hold that skill. Naturally, it was a skill that harnessed the power of the Void.
"Starfall Severance," he moved to the next one, and that, too, was a skill.
He quickly examined all of them, and from the twenty he reviewed, he found that they were all powerful skills that could not be comprehended casually.
"I have two years to learn at least one of these thousand skills," he smiled. "This is pure wickedness. How in the world do they expect me to pick one out of the thousands available?"
There were simply too many skills there, and going through all of them could take months. There was no way he could know all of them without closely examining each one.
"Then again, this is an enlightenment of the Sword Dao. I’m sure there won’t be any weak skills here. But that doesn’t mean I won’t take my time to look into them."
Thus, Kent began examining more tombstones.
He continued without stopping until a month later when he had surprisingly examined about 1,200 tombstones. That was when he decided to pick his first skill and start comprehending it.
"I’ll go for ’Soul Rending Glare’ first. Having the ability to cut someone’s soul is a skill that will come in handy."
With that, he settled his focus on the tombstone for ’Soul Rending Glare’ and injected his energy, immediately entering the skill’s world within the tombstone.
The tombstones are just a means to display the name of the skill and create a pathway for the one trying to learn it to enter the Skill world.
It is some kind of realm that can only be exited when one masters the skill they wanted to learn.
If you couldn’t, then after 2 years, you will be pulled out and out of the realm of enlightenment.
The moment he entered, he appeared in what looked like a shattered sky, with fragments hanging everywhere.
It was a bizarre setting.
Then, from one of the cracks, a red eye as menacing as they come opened, causing Kent’s body to freeze. Suddenly, a powerful energy surged out of it, shattering the very fabric of reality.
"I am inside a soul world where soul attacks can be manifested physically," Kent realized immediately, causing him to look at the eye again as it snapped open and unleashed a second attack.
"I need to see that again." The eye snapped open and unleashed the attack for the second time, causing Kent to raise an eyebrow.
"So that’s what this is. I guess I should watch some more." He sat down and started staring at the eye as it snapped open, unleashed the attack, and then closed immediately.
Every time the eye unleashed an attack, it was as if a part of his understanding clicked, making him realize that the more he watched, the faster his comprehension grew.
A day passed, and the eye executed countless attacks, yet Kent remained seated, gazing at it with intense focus.
A week passed, and before he realized it, two months had gone by. During these two months, Kent did only one thing: he never stopped staring at the eye.
However, a day after two months, a profound energy burst out of his body, and a potent red energy erupted from his eyes, creating ripples that caused the very air to twist and vibrate.
"Success," Kent smiled as he gazed at the now-closed eye.
"I managed to learn it. Now, I must master it and see where it takes me." He smiled, then tapped into the skill and unleashed it again, creating the same ripples.

"This is just great. Three months into my 24-month timeline, and one skill is already down. On to the next, I guess." He closed his eyes, and when he opened them again, he was back to staring at the tombstones.
He quickly went for the skill he had picked as his second.
"Fractured Void," he muttered, smiling.
This skill had something to do with the void. Essentially, with just a stare, Kent could crack open the void like Ingrid and unleash a sword arc that used the void as a channel.
However, there was something unique about it that caught Kent’s attention. The attack that passed through the void could be unleashed in advance—up to 24 hours before the battle.
This meant that if he unleashed the attack hours before the battle, during the fight, he could simply crack the void and let the attack loose.
And it wasn’t limited to just one attack. He could unleash multiple attacks in advance and later bring them out of his own accord.
Now, this was a skill that could not be ignored.
He has some powerful skills he can use. Most are the ones he was using, and more come from his memory of his past life as Jest.

"It’s always fun when everything comes together," a smile appeared on his face as he sent his consciousness into the tombstone and appeared inside a lush mountain range littered with tall, colossal trees.

sentences.text: The sword Dao is a mystery.
Nobody knows how far it extends.
Those who reached the peak of the sword path awakened the Sword Will to its apex, yet they never spoke of its origins or the vastness of its power.
However, it is believed that all Dao stems from the same source, and that source can be accessed through the realm of enlightenment.
It is the only place that one can genuinely say they have met the Dao even if it was just in the will merely in the air.
Everyone experiences enlightenment differently, and each person has eleven chances—or more—to trigger enlightenment at various stages of their path.
Kent triggered his first enlightenment, the [Enlightenment of the Gaze], which came as a surprise.
He never expected it, nor did he anticipate awakening such a power.
Now, he has entered the realm of enlightenment, standing beneath thousands of tombstones.
"Enlightenment, huh?" Kent muttered, gazing at them.
The moment he appeared, he instinctively knew where he was, what he must do, and how long he would remain there.
"Two years to master as many skills as I can...
That’s convenient," Kent smiled.
"Until now, learning how to unleash sword attacks using my eyes wasn’t something I saw coming.
But I guess I must do it.
Two years will pass in the blink of an eye, and as Elsa said, time runs faster here."
He sat down and closed his eyes, sending his consciousness to closely examine the tombstones, each holding a unique skill that cannot be replicated.
The moment he learns a skill, it will vanish, never to return.
"Void Severance," Kent muttered, examining a tombstone that seemed to hold that skill.
Naturally, it was a skill that harnessed the power of the Void.
"Starfall Severance," he moved to the next one, and that, too, was a skill.
He quickly examined all of them, and from the twenty he reviewed, he found that they were all powerful skills that could not be comprehended casually.
"I have two years to learn at least one of these thousand skills," he smiled.
"This is pure wickedness.
How in the world do they expect me to pick one out of the thousands available?"
There were simply too many skills there, and going through all of them could take months.
There was no way he could know all of them without closely examining each one.
"Then again, this is an enlightenment of the Sword Dao.
I’m sure there won’t be any weak skills here.
But that doesn’t mean I won’t take my time to look into them."
Thus, Kent began examining more tombstones.
He continued without stopping until a month later when he had surprisingly examined about 1,200 tombstones.
That was when he decided to pick his first skill and start comprehending it.

If you couldn’t, then after 2 years, you will be pulled out and out of the realm of enlightenment.
