chapters.title: Chapter 394: The Gaze Enlightenment (2)
paragraphs: "This place is nice," Kent muttered, looking around the lush garden he had appeared in. It was a place he immediately took in for he will replicate it inside his Tower.
Suddenly, space cracked, and from the void, a purple eye snapped open. A powerful sword arc—as wide as it could get—flashed out, decimating a tall mountain along with thousands of giant trees.
"Fuck, that is something." A smile appeared on his face, as usual. However, he was shaken, for the attack that had just landed on the mountain was one he could tell was a pure sword slash.
There was no active skill behind it.
It was a pure slash of the sword, utilizing only sword intent and qi. That was all.
Naturally, his passive skill yeh allows him to gain clarity, and one that holds his focus intact activated letting him get enlightened by the attack.
"Is that even possible... Cultivating the act of using just a sword to unleash such an attack?" A seed was planted in his heart. This was something he planned to experiment with.

The attack had decimated the landscape, but he remained unaffected. So he began to stare at the devastation, and from what he observed, Kent—the second skill he had picked—was not as simple as it looked.

"This is going to take some time," he muttered, but there was nothing he could do about that. So he started to watch, and as time passed, he slowly began to grasp the concept—though at a painfully slow pace.

However, while Kent might have been feeling frustrated at his inability to comprehend the skill faster, in reality, someone undergoing a Gaze Enlightenment should, at most, struggle to learn one skill.
Yet he had not only managed to learn one skill already—he was in the process of mastering a second. And if that wasn’t enough, he had gained inspiration from something completely unrelated.
The sword arc that appeared was like a bonus addition to the skill.
Right now, he wasn’t just surpassing expectations—he was shocking many people he wasn’t even aware were alive across the many lives he had lived.
A month later, he still hadn’t fully comprehended the skill. Yet he remained seated for three more months, making it seven months since he had entered the realm of enlightenment.
A few days after spending four months staring at the eye, it finally snapped shut—and his own eyes flew open, creating a small yet visible spatial crack that proved he had indeed mastered the skill.
"I doubt there’s anyone like me out there," he bragged, grinning like an accomplished pirate. But he didn’t leave the space he was in.
No.
Kent began using the skill repeatedly, striving to understand its mechanics more deeply before exiting the realm.
He spent another month inside, mastering the Fractured Void Skill for as long as he could each day—pushing himself until exhaustion set in.
After thirty days, satisfied with his progress, he closed his eyes and left the realm, returning to the space where he could select his third skill.
"I’m sure some people would be furious if they knew I’ve learned two skills from what was supposed to be an impossible task by any standard."
He smirked.
"But what can I say?"

"A wise man once said: when something is given for free and there’s time, don’t look back." Kent closed his eyes, moved past all 1,200 tombstones, and began examining even more to add to his selection.
It took him another month, but he managed to survey an additional 1,250 tombstones, bringing his total to 2,450.
That was when he chose the third skill he would learn.
"Lunar Eclipse Slash."
This skill resembled the sword arc that had appeared while he was comprehending the Fractured Void skill.
It taps into lunar energy, unleashing a red crescent-shaped sword arc imbued with sword qi and intent.
At its core, the skill was a simple sword slash—but its power scaled with mastery. The more Kent refined his understanding, the more devastating it would become.
Satisfied with his choice, Kent sent his consciousness into the tombstone. Like before, he was transported inside—this time to a void of space, surrounded by moons, planets, and stars.
"Hmm, this is unusual," Kent mused. But he couldn’t deny the beauty surrounding him, It was like he had appeared in a domain of beauty yet danger.
Just then, what he had mistaken for a moon suddenly snapped open, revealing a massive red eye.
The instant it opened—just like the previous ones—it unleashed a devastating sword arc that split a star in two.
Kent couldn’t help but grin. It was as silent yet sharp as it can be and he was pleased with that.
"Combining this with Fractured Void... now that’s a recipe for destruction."
His plan was falling perfectly into place.
First, a slash that strikes directly at the soul. Unless the opponent’s soul was stronger—or protected by soul defence—their chances of survival would be zero.
Then there was the Void—something Kent knew he would grow to love, especially since one of his wives was literally made of Void energy.
Now, he was learning an ability that harnessed lunar essence to unleash a sword arc capable of cleaving through planets, moons, and stars.
And the most terrifying part? He wouldn’t wield it with his hand or even a sword. No—this power would be unleashed through his eye.
That alone made it invaluable... and in the wrong hands, catastrophic.
Killing with just a gaze was not something to be underestimated.
Kent began comprehending the skill by observing the eye unleash slash after slash.
Three months later, he grasped its essence—but instead of leaving, he used the remaining time to refine it further, testing whether he could merge it with the Fractured Void skill.
Surprisingly, within a week, he succeeded. For the rest of the year, he honed both skills to perfection. By the time the year ended, he had mastered all three—and was hungry for more.
Eleven months later, he had added four more skills to his arsenal making it seven deadly skills worth fearing.
"I might never return here ever again," he thought. "Why not memorize as many skill names as possible? With my connection to the universe, I might still acquire them later."

A month later, the enlightenment ended, ejecting him from the realm. But he didn’t leave empty-handed—he carried with him seven devastating skills... and the names of 4,500 more waiting to be claimed.

chapters.title: Chapter 395: The Memory Effect
paragraphs: 100 days—that was how long Kent remained inside the enlightenment, according to the tower’s time. However, the moment he opened his eyes, chaotic energy bathed him, threatening to flatten his surroundings.
His body was lifted into the air, and for an entire day, only chaotic sword qi and intent continued to explode from his body.
Slowly, everything calmed down, and he returned to the ground.
The first thing he did was smile at the three lolis smiling back at him. He had no idea the mischief they’d caused.
⟪Congratulations, Master. It looks like you have taken yet another huge leap in your cultivation of the sword path,⟫ Gaia said, and Kent’s smile bloomed.
He had indeed taken a huge leap, and from the look of things, this leap could not be looked down upon.
He had become very powerful, and he could feel it.
"Thank you, Gaia," Kent said.
Of course, while the three ladies were happy for him, part of the reason their happiness showed on their faces was the look on Kent’s face.
Over the course of the last 100 days, they had done their cordial best to decorate his face using markers, and right now, he looked rather funny by all standards.
But he did not know that, so he started checking his strength while the three giggled and laughed about his predicament in their heads.
After mastering the third skill, Kent went ahead and mastered four more, making it seven in total.
That was perhaps the highest number anyone had ever managed to master in any enlightenment.
The fourth skill he mastered was the [Edge of Eternal Night].
It was a rather unique and terrifying sword skill that plunged the battlefield into perpetual night, preventing the opponent from seeing the user’s next attack.
Naturally, Kent didn’t realize how terrifying this skill was until he mastered it.
That was when he saw that using it could easily allow him to land his next attack on an opponent—provided their senses weren’t strong enough to evade while blinded.
Of course, the skill also restricted one’s senses to a certain degree, but if someone possessed a much stronger perception, then it wouldn’t be much of a hassle.
But that was just the fourth skill.
It didn’t have much destructive power, but it was perfect for creating the groundwork for the more powerful skills he would unleash afterwards.
The fifth skill was another that didn’t necessarily deal a destructive blow. However, its stealthy and dangerous nature would make anyone wish it were an active, destructive technique.
Basically, it was the type of skill that, when used would affect the opponent’s perception.
It distorted their senses, making single attacks appear as double or multiple and altering the perceived direction of each strike.
So if a sword slash is coming at their waist, depending on the person’s mental strength, they might see it coming toward their waist or their head.
That was simply too powerful in all aspects, and right now, Kent had mastered such a skill to a stage where he could affect even those several cultivation levels ahead of him.
Then came the sixth skill—a powerful sword move called [Thousand Blades Reflection].
As its name suggested, when used, the opponent would be surrounded by thousands of reflections of any sword move Kent executed.
So if Kent used it on an opponent and unleashed [Rapid Slash], those arcs would multiply into thousands, creating a much more devastating version of the attack.
Strangely, it worked exactly as he had expected. The main attack and the reflections would have the same output and appearance—they are reflections of the same sword move, after all.
However, the disparity between them could still be taken into consideration.
But that wasn’t all. While the reflections mimicked a true attack, Kent could choose to switch them at will, making any of the reflections the real strike.
However, he noticed something the moment he mastered it. It was the effect it had on him.
This skill consumed an immense amount of mental strength, and at his current level, he could use it at most three times in a row before reaching his limit.
But even once was enough for him. The more he grew, the more powerful he became.

The last skill, however, was one that he would have blamed himself for if he had never found it. It was also the reason he dedicated the last month of his time there to learning the names of most of the skills.
The skill’s name was [Dimensional Reflection Slash].
When used, it bent reality, ensuring that every attack from the enemy never reached its target. Instead, the attack was reflected back at the attacker, forcing them to strike themselves.
But there was a catch.

Every attack reflected would have an increase in strength—twice the original power of the attack. It was like taunting an enemy to strike, only to watch them suffer as their own power was turned against them at twice their strength.
However, this skill was also incredibly taxing on his mind.
Plus, not every attack could be reflected. If the attack exceeded his current capabilities, the skill simply wouldn’t work.
Thankfully, he had awakened Sword’s Gaze, which would allow him to recognize which attacks posed a true threat to his life. Those attacks couldn’t be reflected and had to be defended against instead.
But after mastering the skill to some extent and strengthening his mind, he wouldn’t just be able to handle more of these attacks—he could end battles using his enemy’s own power.
Yet, that wasn’t the only thing that had changed.
"I have reached the peak of the Enhanced Sword Qi and Intent stage," Kent muttered, swirling his energy around him.
"Damn, this memory thing is much more powerful than I thought. I can already see this becoming my greatest strength in the coming years."
He didn’t know how this was possible, but he could already sense many changes—one of them being the skill he had just learned while traversing Sword Valley.
Naturally, this filled Kent with confidence, and he turned his gaze toward the Sword Bridge.
"Level Three, here I come."

chapters.title: Chapter 396: Challenging The Third Level of The Sword Bridge
paragraphs: Kent landed on the sword bridge with a sigh, his eyes full of anticipation.
He quickly moved through the first and second levels, which didn’t trigger any challenge, considering he had long dealt with them.
However, the moment he stepped into the third level, a figure clad in blue armor appeared. Of course, it was a copy of him in blue armor.
The clone has blue hair, just like the second level, which had green hair, and the first, which had white hair. This trend suggests that the subsequent ones will also be unique.
However, when the figure appeared, Kent sensed the unfathomable energy surrounding him. He saw the challenge, and it brought a smile to his handsome face.
"This should be fun."
He extended his hand, and his sword appeared in his grip, causing his level nine Enhanced sword intent and qi to explode.
If this was when he battled the second level, he would have felt his energy crashing down hard on them, but this one was different. Its energy was clashing with Kent’s.
’At this level, even Mediocre sword Saints wouldn’t be able to even withstand a strand of my energy.
However, a smile appeared on his face, and it wasn’t one of fear or uncertainty. It was one of expectation.
He may not have had much battle experience... but that was in this life.
His life as Jest was a different ball game. For years, he roamed around in the Sword Valley, facing one danger after another.
That survival instinct, that sixth sense, and that confidence to stand tall had finally become part of him. He had become that confident.
So watching the sword in his hands and the clone before him, he couldn’t help but smile.
Then he moved and unleashed a powerful sword attack aimed right at the heart of the clone. Naturally, the clone crossed its sword over its chest, blocking the attack.
But Kent was a step ahead. He moved to his left and unleashed another sword slash, sending a sword arc at the clone’s left arm.
However, before he could connect that attack, Kent felt the space behind him crack just as the clone swung its sword.
He expected many things, but he never expected a skill he had just learnt to be used this early in battle. But he had to use it because he wanted to see how it worked.
Of course, he was ready for everything, so this didn’t change anything. Instead, his plan remains the same.
"Got ya," he muttered with a smile.

As Kent had planned, the sword arc emerged from the void and landed on the clone’s body, cutting it in half. However, the moment its body was severed, it dispersed into sparkles, revealing it was merely a split body.
This would have caused any human or beast to raise an eyebrow, but before the clone could make a move, thousands of sword arcs appeared in the air, raining down on him.
The sheer force sent the clone flying across the space, landing heavily on the ground. But before it could get back up, Kent unleashed an attack that vanished from sight.
"Fractured Void."
The space cracked open again, and from within the fissure, a powerful sword arc flashed out, severing the clone’s head from its body.
It was a clean cut—perfectly calculated and executed, leaving no room for error.
This time, the clone didn’t use the split body, so the cut was the death blow.
"That was very fun," Kent muttered, watching as the benefits were awarded to him.
At that very moment, his sword skills seemed to have been perfected even further, and his comprehension speed took a significant leap.
Having memories of his past had helped him greatly.
Now, he could already see the end and knew it would be fun regardless of what happened next.
Even before the battle had truly heated up, he had already seen a way to kill the clone, all thanks to the experience from his past life.
His swordsmanship had evolved, and with it, he was already on the path to becoming a monster by the time he fully assimilated his experience.
The memories are his, and he still has two chances to unlock more.
"If that’s the case, doesn’t that mean I can just recall my memories, and that will be all?" Kent muttered.
⟪Master should know that having the memories means learning to improve upon them.
I have just now identified several mistakes you made in that life during your battles, and if you do not improve on them, you will only make them again.

So instead of seeing these memories as a shortcut, see them more like a cheat you can use to correct past mistakes, improve upon them, and add new experiences to them.⟫ Dori, the Mind Weaver, said, making Kent smile.
"That is why you are here, Dori—to help me fix those mistakes. So why don’t we do that now before challenging the fourth level?"
⟪Okay, Master.⟫
Dori wanted to laugh, watching the Guy Fawkes mask they had drawn on Kent’s face, but she knew this was an important moment, so she held back.
But the same couldn’t be said for Gaia and Akira, who were giggling as they watched him.
Dori waved her hand, and 43 scenes appeared in the air. Each scene was a memory of Kent’s past life, showing Jest executing moves that, according to Dori, were flawed.
So they began to work on them.
She was a weaver, so she weaved the correct moves, and based on the weave, Kent would be taught accordingly. Naturally, she was doing everything while Kent sat and assimilated the effects.

Strangely, it wasn’t a tedious process, so they wasted only two hours. By the time she was done, Kent indeed felt he had improved and was now aware of the mistakes he would have made if he had continued using the memories as they were.
But now that he had developed and mastered the fixes, he became much more confident.
"Thank you, Dori." He didn’t forget to show his appreciation.
But the moment that was done, he moved toward the fourth level. The moment he appeared, a new figure emerged. This one was clad in dark armor, just like him.

The only difference was that the clone version of him had dark hair, while his own was purple. Aside from the hair, the clone also wielded a much longer sword than his own, and the Profound sword qi and intent surrounding it were at the third level.
’A level three Profound Sword Qi and Intent.’
"This is just great. A good battle, I see." He smiled, then looked back at himself, who was a clone, before unleashing his aura.
The moment the two clashed, he felt the disparity, which only made him smile more. Then they engaged, and a fierce battle was underway.

chapters.title: Chapter 397: Challenging The Fourth Level of The Sword Bridge
paragraphs: Kent was pushed back, riding the shockwave that exploded after he clashed with the clone.
"Stronger and faster than the third-level clone," he muttered, but he quickly attacked again, aiming to check how fast and precise his attacks had become.
Blades clashed in the air, creating powerful shockwaves and sword flashes that could overwhelm anyone below the Sword Saint stage.
In fact, even Sword Saints with Profound Sword Intent and Qi below the third level would have been overwhelmed, yet he was matching the clone’s attacks.
At every turn, he could tell he wasn’t on par with the clone, but no matter how quick the attack was, he always countered, creating a dynamic he just couldn’t understand.
"Somehow, I can defend against all his attacks like I know when and how they will be executed. This feeling is strange," Kent said to himself as he continued exchanging sword strikes with the clone.
Ten minutes and tens of thousands of sword moves later, something happened that caused Kent to widen his eyes.
"I have matched his speed." He was casually deflecting and parrying the clone’s attacks like it was the most natural thing to do.
In fact, if he were to close his eyes, he would still be able to counter and deflect all the attacks.
"Girls, what is happening?" Kent called his three assistants.
⟪The master is currently experiencing the effect of the Sword Gaze.

Basically, just as you can strengthen your sword and attack with Sword Qi while exerting your influence using Sword Intent, the Sword Gaze helps you adapt to your opponent’s attacks and, to some extent, learn them.

Of course, this requires powerful mental strength. The fact that you have already learned his moves and even assimilated them means your mental strength is extraordinary.⟫ Dori explained, and Kent could only smile.
If Dori’s statement is indeed true, then future battles will be much more interesting. Being able to learn and assimilate his opponent’s moves is something that will go a long way.
"In that case, why not heat things up?" He landed a powerful attack, forcing both of them back.
[Fractured Void]
Kent unleashed one of the Sword Gaze skills, cracking the void behind the clone and forcing out a powerful sword arc.
However, the clone countered by unleashing a powerful beam of red light from its sword. Kent, however, was a step ahead, using a split body to sneak up on the clone.
But just as he closed in, the clone’s split body attacked his split body, creating a powerful shockwave that caused them to annihilate each other.
Kent was startled by what he saw, but he quickly moved again. This time, he unleashed another Sword Gaze skill.
[Edge of Eternal Night]
The clone’s surroundings were plunged into darkness, forcing it to quickly surround itself with a wave of Sword Qi.
But Kent had no intention of moving in, knowing full well that getting closer would be far more dangerous for him.
The Profound Sword Intent in the air was much more dangerous than he thought.
So he chose to overwhelm the clone.
He tapped into [Rapid Slash], unleashing 450 sword arcs.
However, the moment that attack was executed, he channeled even more energy into his sword and unleashed a diagonal sword slash, sending out a powerful sword arc.
The sword arc decimated the Sword Qi vortex the clone had created around its body, allowing the unleashed slash to slam into its torso, sending it flying.
Kent was ready again. Without hesitation, he activated his sneak attacking skii, [Doom Shard], forcing a dark shard to shoot up from the ground, piercing the clone’s chest and killing it.
However, before he could smile, his instincts flared.
He immediately raised his sword overhead just as the clone materialized out of thin air and unleashed a powerful sword move, sending Kent flying backward.
Blood seeped from the corner of his mouth.
Yet, he smiled—this was the peak of battle, the greatest fight he had experienced as a swordsman so far. The previous ones were fun, but this one is peak.
"This is the best." He spat the blood and grinned, showing his red, soaked teeth.
He moved, his speed blinding, as he began unleashing sword arcs while dashing across the battlefield.
The clone countered and defended, their movements resembling two phantoms clashing at impossible speeds.
Kent was using [Phantom Mirage Blades] to distort the clone’s perception, but the clone countered with the exact same skill.
The perfect counter to this technique was itself, and Kent was struggling to come up with the best move to kill the clone at the moment.
Any skill he used was countered by the clone using the same skill, making this much more interesting yet annoying.
However, the longer they fought, the more he learned. And at this moment, he was pushing himself to the absolute limit—just to see how far he could go.
An hour later, he started to bleed, and the clone also had cuts on its body, meaning they had both sustained wounds.
But within that hour, Kent had found a way to win.
"Here we go."
He blinked back and used [Thousand Blades Reflection] to multiply his [Rapid Slash] skill, causing thousands of sword arcs to appear. Then, he moved away and used it again.
This forced the clone to take drastic measures to defend against the relentless assault.
Before the clone could finish defending, Kent moved into position and unleashed a skill he had never used before. Of course it was a skill he had just learned thanks to Jest.
"Limitless Sword Arc Domain."

The moment the skill activated, Kent felt the 100-meter radius around him grow razor-sharp. Then, he looked toward the clone, which was consumed by thousands of tiny sword arcs, slicing into it relentlessly.
He wanted to unleash more sword techniques, but before he could move, he sensed his energy draining rapidly—like something was siphoning it away.
The depletion was so fast that he had to quickly deactivate the skill.
But the job was nearly done—the clone had been reduced to a pitiful state.
Using the last of his energy, he unleashed one final swing of his sword, sending a powerful sword arc that cleaved the clone in half.
This time, no split body appeared, meaning he had successfully killed the fourth-level clone, clearing the level.
"This skill is not something I can use at this moment," Kent thought to himself as he sat down, placing his sword beside him.
A few seconds later, his fatigue faded, and all his wounds healed completely.

chapters.title: Chapter 398: Back To Gaiaville
paragraphs: "Why are you ladies smiling?" Kent asked right when he appeared in the Tower City, where the ladies, including Alina, spent time together.
He came to the city right after defeating the 4th level of the Sword Bridge.
Of course, he had a few chats with the three Lolis, and per their deduction, the [Limitless Sword Arcs Domain] skill shouldn’t be used now, but he needed it.
At most, he should start using it when he becomes a Root Ascension stage expert. The three-second activation just a few minutes ago drained him completely.
Had he not acted quickly, he would have passed out. This means the requirement to use it was just too much for the current him.
In fact, in his memories, Jest only used it three times, but he was a Peak Transcendent back then, so the exhaustion wasn’t that much.
So he left and came to spend some time with his ladies. But the moment he appeared, they started laughing at him.
They started laughing at him as if he had wet himself. However, he was confident he hadn’t, which meant something else was amiss, and he ought to know.
So he asked.
"Nothing. We just want to say that this new look is perfect for you," Selene giggled, watching Kent’s face now resemble a blend of white, black, and red masks.
The three lolis who had spent quite some time on his face were now smiling somewhere in the city.
"What look?" He also knew that if he had become more handsome, the ladies would be blushing right now, so the fact that they were smiling meant something different.
So, he waved his hand, and a mirror appeared.
"What the f..." Kent almost screamed his heart out when he saw what had become of his face.
"Gaia," he called out, but for the first time, the cosmic loli didn’t appear. Instead, she and her sisters held their stomachs, laughing their lungs out.
"I will punish you three," Kent muttered, but a small smile appeared on his face. The ladies were also smiling as they helped him move to a fountain and wash the design off his face.
"It looks like the three young ladies are much more unruly than we are. Maybe we should learn from them," Val said, and Kent just shrugged.
"I will punish them for that." The ladies knew he was just making that up.
They could clearly see how much he liked those three small humans and how much they also cherished him, even if they claimed they were just assistants.
They saw how resourceful they were when Kent was in a coma after his battle with Evil Bat, so this was their way of telling him they were always there for him.
Kent turned to Nara, who was wearing a rather provocative gown that was showing more than it was hiding. He raised his eyebrow.
"You like what you see?" Nara asked strangely, causing Kent to smile.
"If I said no, I’d want you to lock me up and give me a good beating," the upcoming Night Rider smiled. Though the idea was already planted in her head, she still wanted to know more about Kent.
But aside from that, Nara was on the same wavelength as Selene.
They were both shameless and seductive in their own styles.
Selene tended to make everything about sex, while Nara—about whom not much was known—had a way of making men question whether they were the boss in the relationship or if she was.

Before her unfortunate incident sixty-plus years ago, many men had tried to court her, but after just one meeting, they would all lose interest, realizing that the lady they were pursuing wasn’t someone who could be won over with their usual simp lines.
Nara was different. She was lively, easygoing, and very annoying.
Mara won Kent about her, but now that he was seeing it, he couldn’t help but plan to crack that which couldn’t be broken before.

"You should stick around some more. Maybe you’ll get lucky one of these days," she smiled at him, but Kent just shook his head and turned to Zaila, who was now blushing when Kent’s eyes landed on her.
"No need to be shy. The fact that you are with them means they wouldn’t let you live a chaste life," he laughed, causing his ladies to roll their eyes.
As if they aren’t helping him get himself another beauty destined to become a powerhouse despite her setback.
The atmosphere was very calm and lovely.
They had already spent over a hundred days inside the city while Kent was undergoing his enlightenment, so it was safe to say that the trauma the ladies had experienced had diminished significantly.
But that was to be expected, considering the place they were in could make anyone forget all about their worries.
Zaila even started training again with her master, for she wanted to get much stronger so she would never fall into such a situation again, like she did with the sect master.
According to her account of what happened twenty-plus years ago, she was attacked by the sect master sneakily, but she managed to dodge and retaliate.
However, she was overpowered after exchanging a few blows with the sect master. This was her greatest failure, for when her life was truly in danger, she couldn’t even escape.
So, she started training, and thankfully, she was now surrounded by powerful warriors with whom she could train.
Nara had spent her time every day doing the things she wanted to do with her sisters all these years, so she hadn’t touched a weapon yet.
But she knew it was only a matter of time, for she could already sense it. Her duty was calling, and when Kent appeared just now, she knew that duty must be answered first.
"Alina, when did you get here?" Kent asked, smiling.
Lady Lani had been keeping her close the past few days on the outside, so she hadn’t had much time inside the tower like her sisters.
She also hadn’t started her training yet.
"She has entered seclusion for a few days, so that’s how I got to come here. But I don’t mind staying outside with her. She is much more fun, you know," Alina replied.
"Good to know you were having fun. But why don’t we spend some time here and enjoy ourselves together?
The Pill Master competition is two days away so we have more time on our hands here." The ladies nodded and dragged him away into a large pool where things started to heat up.
Nara and Zaila were blushing as they watched the purple-haired youngster get intimate with his ladies right in front of them.

Of course, they were still in their almost transparent swimwear, which was normal to them considering they had seen them wear it the past few weeks, but what was making them blush was the actions happening.
"You ladies still know we are here, right?" Nara said.
"We know, but if you can’t hold on anymore, you might as well join us." Selene smiled at them as Kent wrapped his lips around her nipple and started sucking on it while Ingrid stroked his dick.
Zaila was the first to turn away as her cheeks burned red. Nara, on the other hand, was smiling, but her eyes — that dreamy look in her eyes — were telling a different story.

They saw how resourceful they were when Kent was in a coma after his battle with Evil Bat, so this was their way of telling him they were always there for him.

He raised his eyebrow.
"You like what you see?" Nara asked strangely, causing Kent to smile.

Nara was different.
She was lively, easygoing, and very annoying.
Mara won Kent about her, but now that he was seeing it, he couldn’t help but plan to crack that which couldn’t be broken before.
"You should stick around some more.
Maybe you’ll get lucky one of these days," she smiled at him, but Kent just shook his head and turned to Zaila, who was now blushing when Kent’s eyes landed on her.
"No need to be shy.
The fact that you are with them means they wouldn’t let you live a chaste life," he laughed, causing his ladies to roll their eyes.
As if they aren’t helping him get himself another beauty destined to become a powerhouse despite her setback.
The atmosphere was very calm and lovely.
They had already spent over a hundred days inside the city while Kent was undergoing his enlightenment, so it was safe to say that the trauma the ladies had experienced had diminished significantly.
But that was to be expected, considering the place they were in could make anyone forget all about their worries.
Zaila even started training again with her master, for she wanted to get much stronger so she would never fall into such a situation again, like she did with the sect master.
According to her account of what happened twenty-plus years ago, she was attacked by the sect master sneakily, but she managed to dodge and retaliate.
However, she was overpowered after exchanging a few blows with the sect master.
This was her greatest failure, for when her life was truly in danger, she couldn’t even escape.
So, she started training, and thankfully, she was now surrounded by powerful warriors with whom she could train.
Nara had spent her time every day doing the things she wanted to do with her sisters all these years, so she hadn’t touched a weapon yet.
But she knew it was only a matter of time, for she could already sense it.
Her duty was calling, and when Kent appeared just now, she knew that duty must be answered first.
"Alina, when did you get here?" Kent asked, smiling.
Lady Lani had been keeping her close the past few days on the outside, so she hadn’t had much time inside the tower like her sisters.
She also hadn’t started her training yet.
"She has entered seclusion for a few days, so that’s how I got to come here.
But I don’t mind staying outside with her.

chapters.title: Chapter 399: Night Riders First Secret
paragraphs: After the public display of intimacy inside the pool, Kent and the ladies started spending time inside the city. He had promised them he would come and spend time with them, so he did.
They had fun and ate a lot of good food.
They did a lot of sucking and licking, which left them craving more. Naturally, the tower is a place where they have more than enough time to do a lot of things.
Since they have gained new bodies, their second yet first time will also be in the most romantic settings.
The three who had yet to get intimate with him were also now prepared, and right after the awakening ritual of the fourth Night Rider, they would have their moment with him.
But every good thing comes to an end, so after ten days, they left the city and returned to the Legion Tower, where Uncle Drew was waiting.
The moment they appeared there, and Nara set her sights on Uncle Drew, a sense of familiarity washed over her, causing her to ask:
"Have we met before?"
"As a matter of fact, yes. We did meet before, 68 years ago to be exact. However, what you are feeling now isn’t because of that; it’s more about what is about to happen to you.
I know you can hear the call, and soon, that call must be answered," Uncle Drew said before turning to look at Kent.
"Young Master, with your permission, I can start the process," Uncle Drew said, and Kent nodded.
"Before we start anything, do you have any questions you would want answers to? I know this is all strange to you, but I think you have some questions you need to ask."
"What would I become?" she asked. She could feel it deep in her bones. The changes that are coming would change her, so she wants to know.
"You will become an existence known as a Night Rider. Most would call you Riders of the Night or the Night Warden. And as a Night Rider, you are neither dead nor alive, for you hang in the middle.

You will become an invincible being in the night and have supreme authority over the flames of hell. You will also have insight into the supernatural, and if you once were, then you will be again," Uncle Drew explained.
"If you once were, then you will be again. Can you explain this part?"
"It sounds exactly as it means. The Night Riders were beings who fought in these universes, but we all died."
Kent raised an eyebrow. "This is new information," he said. He had asked before, but Uncle Drew knew little to nothing about who he was or what any of this meant.
"Yes. You remember that Queen of the Underworld I told you about?" Uncle Drew asked.
"Nyx..." Strangely, Kent had always had this name on his lips since he first heard it.
"Yes. According to her, when we met in the Underworld, I am something of an incarnation of the first Night Rider. And yes, she knew I was a Night Rider before I even told her.
But after spending a few years working with her, I found out a small part of the truth. We Night Riders are indeed incarnations of our past selves.
I tried to understand how we came into being, but she said only some ancient book — one that takes one’s longevity when read — could disclose that.
She also said every Night Rider is still born with their memories locked within them, and it will take some time to start recalling them.

But she helped me unlock a very small portion of mine. This was the reason I slowly went from Root Sage to Transcendent. I discovered a secret from my past as a Night Rider, and the effect was what you saw."
Kent smiled, for he understood where he was coming from. He himself had grown by leaps and bounds after his second memory recovery, so he knew Uncle Drew was telling the truth.
But while he was smiling, he still couldn’t figure out who this Nyx lady was or why she was going out of her way to help his subordinate.
Of course, there wasn’t an answer to his question now, but he was bound to find out in the coming years.
Nara listened to Uncle Drew talk about the Night Riders, and at every turn, something within her seemed to want to awaken.
"Another question. Would becoming a Night Rider separate me from my sister forever?" Her biggest fear now was being away from her sister.
She wanted to spend the rest of her life with her sister and new friends if possible.
"No. Though you will become a Night Rider, you can stay with your sister until we have a mission to embark on. However, the moment there is a mission, there should be no excuse.
So for now, your mission is to protect the young master."
She nodded.
These conditions were excellent in her eyes. She liked the fact that she could stay by her sister’s side and only leave if there was a mission.
"But don’t worry too much. I will be away for nearly two years, so you will have more time to stay with your sister daily, especially if they are spent inside the tower space."
"Okay. This is indeed perfect for me. And don’t worry; I will not neglect my duties," Nara said, making the rest of the ladies smile.
They knew what was about to happen the moment she accepted her destiny. They wanted to see what would become of her after she awakened to her True Name.

They had all witnessed how amazing and dangerous their own awakenings were, but afterward, they became incredible women. Now, they wanted to see what would become of their sister the moment she awakened.
After saying that, Uncle Drew nodded.
"In that case, we can start the process now." Uncle Drew touched her forehead and muttered some words. A few seconds later, the sky above them started turning.
⟪I call dibs on another dragon⟫ Lilian said through the harem connection.
⟪I say a wolf⟫ Ingrid added, and just like that, the rest started speculating. Lilian had come out as a dragon, and Ingrid as a Voidling.
So they were all eager to see what kind of race she would be awakening as. They gave their predictions, leaving only one person.
⟪Sister Selene, what do you think?⟫ Ingrid asked.
⟪Judging by the color of the clouds, I’d say she will be coming out as a wraith⟫.
The sisters shook their heads, hearing such a nonserious answer from her.

chapters.title: Chapter 400: Veyrha, The Twilight Brand (1)
paragraphs: Vey, a child born in the night, was destined to command the night.
Born to a scholar mother and a warrior father, she was the popular child among her peers. She had her mother’s status to lean on and her father’s warrior spirit to brag about.
She was lazy but very interesting to be around.
They called her the True Princess, for in their empire, she had more fame than most princesses.
Of course, she didn’t care what name she was called, for her only reason for living was to make her parents happy.

Her studies were good, and she picked up the sword when she came of age. But in her heart, she never truly wanted to be a warrior or become a scholar. If possible, she would forever be free and do as she pleased.
But destiny said otherwise.
It was a bleak night, one unlike any other. The shallow night changed everything for her.
Years before Ebonviel appeared in the universe, there were rumors of it.
Many called it the First Universe, some called it the Mini Universe, and others called it the Dead Universe. But on the 14th moon of the Ebon Year, the veil broke, and darkness descended.
That was the day Vey saw true darkness, and among the millions who saw it, she was the only one fascinated by it.
The dark depth gazing at her was a breathtaking sight for her.
The veil cracked, and the battle between Kael Duskbane, a being wielding two longswords and riding on the back of a death horse, and a Dreadknight began.
The battle broke the veil that separated the known universe from Ebonviel, the world of true darkness where Raveth, the Wraith Queen, ruled.
Kael was her right-hand man, a warrior unlike any other. The battle lasted for an hour until the Dreadknight was drowned against the relentless onslaught of Kael’s dual blades.

That day, after the battle was over and Kael was leaving, he turned and stared at one person. That person was Vey, who, from that very moment, found the motivation she needed to pick up the sword again.
She started to train, and before long, she began to shock everyone around her. Soon, those who heard of her began to spread her legend.
Thousands of years passed, and Vey reached a stage in swordsmanship where even the so-called sword geniuses of her world could only bow in surrender.
But to Vey, she never truly desired any of this, for the only reason she was training was for when the veil opened again. She wanted to enter that place.
Yet, for thousands of years, the veil remained closed—until it finally opened, when the Realm of Ebonviel was in distress. Kael came for her.
The forbidden legend has it that for 1,022 days, a great battle rocked Ebonviel when the Wraith Queen was betrayed by her second general.
They fought, and in the end, the Wraith Queen was forced to make a huge sacrifice for the future of what she was destined to protect.
Legend has it that when the battle was nearing its end, the Wraith Queen gazed at the 66 individuals who acted as her weapons and killed for her.
Vey was one of the 66, for she fought and killed to her heart’s content. But in the end, they still lost—or were on track to lose.
The Wraith Queen was stabbed in the back and was destined to die, for there was nothing that could save her.
The Wraith Queen looked at the 66, and a rare smile appeared.
"I was told a day like this would come—the day I would fall and my legend would come to an end. But you know me, I am stubborn and never truly listened to things like that.
But I guess this is the end.
However, I am not sad because, at this moment, I have 66 amazing people I can call family. You all proved to me that despite my distant lifestyle, I can still have friends and a family.
This is a blessing to a person like me.
This is why I won’t listen to fate again and will do as I please.

I saw what follows, but I cannot, in good conscience, die and leave you all to face that danger. So, before I die, I will leave something behind—something that, one day in the future, will make sense."
She slashed her chest open and stabbed her hand into the wound, retrieving her crystal heart.
"This is the Mark of the Night, but I will call it the Heart of the Night Riders. You all are creatures of the night, and so I will make you creatures who can harness the power of the night.
Your legend will end soon, and it will be hidden from everyone. But one day will come when the legend of the Night Riders will spread across worlds and encompass the entire universe.
Go, and let your name be known by many, for when the night comes and you open your eyes, no weapon in existence can kill you."
The sky inside the tower shook, and at once, eternal darkness enveloped everything, preventing everyone except Nara, Uncle Drew, Saden, and Kent from seeing what followed next.
Up in the air, Nara was moved deeper into the clouds, where a dark, colossal head of a wraith appeared. Then it moved and swallowed her whole.
"That is a wraith, right?" Kent asked, and Uncle Drew nodded.
"That is a wraith, young master. They are creatures of legend. From what I know about them, they command the night, for they are creatures born from the night.
Many legends even say that they were once the true overlords of the beasts, for they can’t easily be killed, especially at night."
"I see," Kent nodded, staring at the events in the dark clouds, which were exuding a rather powerful energy.
"If my calculations are correct, then she is being reborn as a wraith-human hybrid," Uncle Drew smiled.
This smile was because of something he discovered. In the small memory he had remembered, he saw Nara in it. That day, when he saw her, he knew she was someone he shared destiny with.
Now, staring at her, he could only smile and wait for the outcome.
